correctness.rationale: For a fixed-order finite graph, every derangement is independently enumerated, every legal swap generated and checked, and all graph edges verified reversible. Conjugation by S9 is an automorphism, giving precisely eight relevant cycle-type orbits. Breadth-first search from each representative reaches all 133496 states and produces the claimed eccentricities. The unique distance-ten vertex from the (3,3,3) representative equals its inverse; conjugation transfers the classification to all 2240 such states, giving 1120 unordered pairs. Independent C++ lexicographic and Python recursive matching enumerators agree on all eight distance profiles and bounds; an explicit ten-move witness is checked. Finite exhaustive proof does not claim results for any other order.

originality.rationale: The exact same legal two-position swap derangement graph is treated by Jain (2021), but its connectivity, valency, vertex connectivity, and spanning walks do not imply the exact nine-symbol diameter, complete eccentricity profile, or classification of 1120 unique-inverse antipodal pairs. Dyer–Jerrum–Müller (2015) study the matching switch chain, with a chordal-bipartite diameter bound inapplicable to the nine-crown graph. Searches of exact claims, synonymous transformations, covering theorems, sequence databases and pertinent public research results produced no equivalent claim. Priority remains qualified by inaccessible and unindexed literature.

value.rationale: Exact worst-case switch distance and extremal matching pairs are natural precise questions for a canonical bipartite perfect-matching Markov chain on crown graphs. The result distinguishes ten-step antipodal inverse triple-three-cycles from all other states at distance at most nine and exhibits a nonuniform eccentricity spectrum; the facts are not deductions from known connectivity and degree bounds, and offer a meaningful reproducible exact benchmark for local reconfiguration algorithms. No generalization or random-walk mixing claim is asserted.
